meta.title: How it works · yokoten
meta.description: Follow one task from you to the server: the lead, a desk worker in its own sandbox, the guard before each action, and the checks when it lands.

intro.label: How it works
intro.title: One task, step by step
intro.body: Press Play, or go one step at a time with Next. Each tag is one piece of data moving.

player.label: Current step
player.ready: Ready. Press Play, or Next to go one step at a time.
player.red: stopped, failed, or waits for you

steps: You give the lead a task.
The lead asks the model. yokoten doesn't read this.
The lead opens a desk. The guard checks it first.
yokoten opens the desk: its own clone, in a sandbox.
The worker asks the model. Only the model API gets out.
The worker tries to push. The guard stops it.
The worker edits a file. The guard lets it through.
It commits, and the commit check runs in the sandbox.
The desk runs the tests in the sandbox: evidence.
The lead closes the desk and gets the evidence.
The lead reviews the diff and runs the checks itself.
The lead opens a PR. It touches guard settings, so the guard asks you (coming).
With your yes, the PR goes to the server.
Round 1: the lead checks CI. It failed.
The lead fixes it and pushes again, through the guard.
Round 2: the lead checks CI. It passed.
The lead merges, then tells you.

items.q: My agent already has a sandbox. Why use yokoten's?
items.a: Each vendor's sandbox is different, and it only locks commands. A desk locks the whole worker the same way, whatever its vendor.
No. Inside a desk, the yokoten sandbox replaces the agent's own.

items.q: Can a worker come from any vendor?
items.a: Yes: Claude Code, Codex, Grok or Muse.
